author: WP01
summary: Maps CNA's sibling repositories (sharp-runtime, easy-gl, free-direct, xna4-spec, cna-samples, cna-examples), how CMake wires them, and each sibling's own boundary. The wiring is current (with a new CNA_SHARP_RUNTIME_ROOT override and reworded messages); several sibling facts are stale (sharp-runtime scope, plan statuses, sample counts, cna-examples maturity, easy-gl's MIGRATION.md). The site had the sibling checkout rules; the per-sibling boundaries, xna4-spec's real role and the consumer distinction were missing and are on the new ecosystem page, with the figure recreated and corrected.

concepts.section: Ecosystem and Vocabulary
concepts.text: Most siblings are expected as literal sibling directories (../sharp-runtime, ../easy-gl, ...) because CNA's CMake looks for them there; the organisation named in CNA's clone hints is the older openeggbert one.

target.evidence: CMakeLists.txt; cmake/RendererSelection.cmake; cna, sharp-runtime and cna-samples moved to the libcna organisation (fact sheet 08), free-direct stays in openeggbert

concepts.section: The dependency graph
concepts.text: The ecosystem table: sharp-runtime (C++ subset of the .NET BCL, foundation), easy-gl (OpenGL/ES wrapper for the five EasyGL profiles), free-direct (DirectDraw/DirectSound/DirectPlay subset for FREEDIRECT), xna4-spec (XML spec for audits), cna-samples and cna-examples (end-to-end consumers).

target.evidence: roles confirmed at the sibling revisions in the table; xna4-spec is not used by CNA's census (tools/audit_xna_runtime_surface.py reads Microsoft XML/DLL metadata)

concepts.section: The dependency graph
concepts.text: Every sibling is an independent, separately buildable and tested project, neither vendored nor a submodule; sharp-runtime names CNA as its consumer and could serve a project unrelated to XNA.
tokens: None of these is vendored into CNA or included as a Git submodule

target.evidence: CMakeLists.txt comment (sibling, not submodule); .gitmodules has no sibling entries; no pin/lock file at TARGET

concepts.section: The sibling build graph
concepts.text: Each sibling check is an if(NOT EXISTS .../CMakeLists.txt) guard that fails configuration with a copy-pasteable fix in the message rather than a later missing-header error.

target.evidence: CMakeLists.txt: the sharp-runtime path is now the overridable cache variable CNA_SHARP_RUNTIME_ROOT and the message reads 'Missing sharp-runtime checkout at ...'

concepts.section: The sibling build graph
concepts.text: sharp-runtime is added unconditionally; easy-gl and free-direct are pulled in only for a matching renderer, so an SDL_RENDERER or VULKAN build never checks for them.
tokens: never looks for easy-gl or free-direct

target.evidence: cmake/RendererSelection.cmake (GL identities add ../easy-gl once; FREEDIRECT adds ../free-direct)

concepts.section: The sibling build graph
concepts.text: free-direct is not a leaf: its CMake adds a third sibling, free-api, and both resolve SDL3, SDL3_image and SDL3_mixer from CNA's already-vendored targets so the chain shares one SDL3 build; free-eggbert and planetblupi are further consumers of free-direct.

concepts.section: sharp-runtime: the floor CNA stands on
concepts.text: Anything CNA needs from .NET is added to sharp-runtime first and then used from CNA; .NET concepts are never inlined into CNA headers as raw C++ types or ad-hoc workarounds.

concepts.section: sharp-runtime: the floor CNA stands on
concepts.text: sharp-runtime is explicitly not a CLR and is described as lacking reflection, GC, delegates beyond std::function, serialization, P/Invoke and a full cryptography/TLS stack.
tokens: organised as independently selectable CMake components
without attempting to implement a CLR

target.evidence: sharp-runtime@41b918c9 README.md: not a CLR/JIT/GC, but its scope now includes XML serialisation, networking and HTTP, tasks and non-encryption cryptography

concepts.section: sharp-runtime: the floor CNA stands on
concepts.text: sharp-runtime tracks porting status per .NET type in plan.sqlite3 (committed despite an ignore rule) with states todo, ported, ignore/ignored and tobedecided.

target.evidence: sharp-runtime@41b918c9 plan.sqlite3 table task: 16,207 rows = ported 1,087, ignore 140, ignored 14,980; no todo or tobedecided rows remain

concepts.section: easy-gl: OpenGL without a windowing opinion
concepts.text: easy-gl is a toolkit-independent C++20 wrapper over OpenGL/ES that owns no window, context or event loop: the host creates and activates the context and supplies a GetProcAddress-style loader.

target.evidence: easy-gl@deda7a42 README.md (Architecture boundaries); CMakeLists.txt links meta-gl::meta-gl

concepts.section: easy-gl: OpenGL without a windowing opinion
concepts.text: Calling code gates GL-only features away from GL ES through device.supports(...)/require(...); easy-gl calls its own scope a compact vertical slice exercised by hello-triangle-sdl and two smoke-test suites, and CNA's EasyGL renderer grew far beyond it.

concepts.section: easy-gl: OpenGL without a windowing opinion
concepts.text: easy-gl's MIGRATION.md described nine already-landed signature changes in future tense, a sibling instance of documentation outliving the moment it was accurate.
concepts.note: Historical documentation anecdote; MIGRATION.md no longer exists at easy-gl deda7a42, so nothing current remains.

concepts.section: free-direct: DirectX 3 scoped to two legacy games
concepts.text: free-direct is a deliberately narrow, game-driven subset of 2D-era DirectX (DirectDraw, DirectSound, DirectPlay) over SDL3, aimed at running specific legacy games; its non-goals are full DirectX compatibility, hardware-accurate emulation, a Direct3D pipeline and APIs the games do not call.

concepts.section: free-direct: DirectX 3 scoped to two legacy games
concepts.text: free-direct backs CNA's FREEDIRECT renderer and has real DirectPlay networking over an optional ENet transport.

concepts.section: free-direct: DirectX 3 scoped to two legacy games
concepts.text: free-direct's tests are split by transport: the default ctest exercises the loopback transport's synchronous semantics, the ENet tests are selected with the enet label, and running the unfiltered suite on an ENet build fails one loopback-scoped test by design.

concepts.section: xna4-spec: a ground truth to audit against
concepts.text: xna4-spec is a machine-readable XML transcription of the XNA 4.0 documentation (every type with member descriptions; 544 types in 19 namespaces) whose stated purpose includes auditing C++ reimplementations.

target.evidence: xna4-spec@fedc17aa index.xml (544 types) and 19 namespace directories; its README says 550

concepts.section: xna4-spec: a ground truth to audit against
concepts.text: A dated 227-of-245 FNA-type presence audit in CNA's release prose used FNA's type list as denominator, not xna4-spec; TARGET's generated census closes at 331/331 types and 3,627/3,627 members, and neither number is behavioural coverage.

target.evidence: CHANGELOG.md (alpha.1 entry); docs/xna-4-runtime-member-coverage.md; CNA code/CI never reference xna4-spec

concepts.section: cna-samples and cna-examples: two different kinds of proof
concepts.text: cna-samples ports the official XNA Game Studio 4.0 samples under Ms-PL and asks whether CNA runs real historical XNA code; its plan counts 153 archive entries as 63 completed, 23 placeholders and 67 exclusions.
concepts.note: The site's pinned figures replace the Bible's older catalogue statuses; the question each repository answers is kept.

target.evidence: cna-samples@4da98a0 (site canon): 153 directories, 87 complete, 40 playable, 49 awaiting owner decisions, 14 non-ports

concepts.section: cna-samples and cna-examples: two different kinds of proof
concepts.text: cna-examples is original MIT-licensed work, an Ensemble-inspired single application browsing Area/Category/Demo, described as an early skeleton whose demo screens were not yet implemented and which targeted only the EasyGL family.

target.evidence: cna-examples@ea33c9a2 README.md: 13 areas, 79 categories, 249 demo screens, verified on OPENGLES3 and SDL_RENDERER

concepts.section: Repositories mentioned but out of this book's scope
concepts.text: The wider organisation hosts CNA-adjacent projects (cna-template, cna-extended, cna-craft), other graphics libraries (meta-gl, easy-3d), games and tools built on the stack (mesh-craft, galaxy-eggbert, free-eggbert, planetblupi, mobile-eggbert) and documentation sites.

concepts.section: Repositories mentioned but out of this book's scope
concepts.text: The book limits its scope to the six repositories CNA's build, README and porting rules name directly.

figures.note: Recreated as a text diagram and corrected: the census input is Microsoft's XML/DLL metadata (xna4-spec is only a searchable inventory, not used by CNA's tools), FNA and the Wine+DXVK XNA oracle are shown as evidence inputs, and consumers are shown as pinning their own CNA revision.
